## Third Verse
<!--Put the first two verses of The Walrus and the Carpenter here!-->
there’s a bluebird in my heart that   
wants to get out   
but I’m too tough for him,   
I say, stay in there, I’m not going   
to let anybody see    
you.   

there’s a bluebird in my heart   
that wants to get out   
but I pour whiskey on him and inhale   
cigarette smoke  
and the whores and the bartenders   
and the grocery clerks   
never know that  
he’s  
in there.     

## Last Verse
statistics begins at seven    
which already feels statistically unfair.  
the professor writes symbols on the board   
like he’s sending threats from another dimension.  
mean, median, mode—  
three little words pretending to be harmless.  
then probability walks in  
and ruins everybody’s evening.  
I stare at the numbers  
and the numbers stare back.  
somewhere, a bell curve is laughing at me.  
the guy beside me understands everything  
which makes him suspicious.  
I punch formulas into my calculator  
like feeding coins into a broken slot machine.  
sometimes the answer comes out right.  
most times, it doesn’t.  
but I keep showing up,  
because apparently there is a chance I’ll pass,  
and statistics says a chance is still a chance.
